steps.path: The pencil at the right end of the status bar
steps.headline: Which row style should "pick what shows" menus use?
steps.notice: The row style you pick here becomes the one for every "pick what shows" menu. Both new versions: each group is a small label over a card (the guide's "a label first, nothing bare"), and each row shows a one-line hint under its name instead of an (i) you have to press. The theme cycle is a fold under the Theme row instead of a pencil. References: Settings → Sound and Performance use the same switch rows; the tick box is the one in Tags & note.

variants.label: Today
variants.summary: Bare tick boxes under small labels, an (i) on every row.

variants.label: Switches on the right
variants.summary: Each row is name and hint on the left, a switch on the right, like the switches in Settings. The always-on four say "Always shown" instead of a switch.
variants.risk: Taller rows, so more scrolling: about 8 rows show at once instead of 13.

variants.label: Tick boxes on the left
variants.summary: The same cards and hints, with a tick box on the left of each name; the whole row is the click target.
variants.risk: The same extra height; the greyed ticks on the always-on four can read as "broken" rather than "fixed".

steps.path: The "Always on" group at the top
steps.headline: Should the four always-on items still be listed as rows?
steps.today: Model, Permissions, Tags & note and Announcements are listed first with ticks you can't change.
steps.problem: Four rows that can't be changed take the top of the menu, above the things you came to change.

options.label: One line instead
options.summary: A short line at the top: "Model, permissions, tags & note and announcements are always shown."
pros: The menu starts with things you can change.
cons: The four lose their one-line explanations.

options.label: Keep the rows
pros: Every item in the bar is explained in one place.

steps.path: The pencil at the end of the chip row above the message box
steps.headline: How should the quick chips editor work?
steps.today: White rows with each chip's name and the start of its message, and an ✕ to remove. You can't change the order, and long messages are cut off.
steps.problem: Its rows don't match any other menu, you can't reorder chips, and you can't read what a chip will send.
steps.proposal: Two ways, both in a labelled card like the status bar editor.

options.label: Rows that open to edit
options.summary: Each chip is a row: name, with its full message as the hint underneath. Click a row to edit both in place; a drag handle on the left reorders; a remove icon on the right.
pros: See exactly what each chip sends.
cons: Taller rows when messages are long.

options.label: Restyle only
options.summary: Same rows and ✕, moved into a card; no reordering, no editing.
cons: Still can't reorder or edit a chip.

steps.path: A session's tag chip → Tags & note, and its "Manage tags…"
steps.headline: Should Tags & note and Manage tags become one popup?
steps.today: Tags & note ticks tags onto this session and holds its note. Renaming, recolouring, archiving or deleting a tag happens in a second popup, Manage tags, with text boxes and two buttons on every row.
steps.problem: You said both need rebuilding. Two popups for one list of tags, and Manage tags' rows are busy.

options.label: One popup
options.summary: One list: tick a tag to put it on this session; a "…" on each row renames, recolours, archives or deletes it. The note is its own labelled card below. Manage tags goes away.
pros: Everything about tags in one place.
Rows stay quiet until you open the "…".
cons: Rename and delete sit one click from the tick you use every day.

options.label: Keep two, restyle both
options.summary: Tags & note and Manage tags both get the new cards and rows; Manage tags' rows show the name with a "…" instead of text boxes and buttons.
pros: Renaming and deleting stay out of the way of everyday tagging.
